Executive Summary
On 2025 May 12, Rose Hall (Developments) Limited (RHDL) made an application to the Office
of Utilities Regulation (OUR), for an Annual Price Adjustment Mechanism (ANPAM)
adjustment of 3.62%, to be applied to its sewerage rates.
This adjustment is in keeping with the requirements specified in the Rose Hall utilities
Company Limited - Sewerage Rate Determination, Document Number
WAS2011002_DET002, which addresses the application of the Price Adjustment Mechanism
(PAM), and its relationship to the National Water Commission's (NWC's) Price Adjustment
Mechanism
The PAM is applied to customers' bills monthly. The mechanism allows for an adjustment of
base rates by rolling in the cumulative monthly PAM rate into the base rates. This process
generally occurs on an annual basis. The annual reset is referred to as the Annual Price
Adjustment Mechanism (ANPAM).
RHDL's ANPAM mirrors that of the NWC. The adjustment is applicable to customers' 2025 May
consumption, which will be reflected in the 2025 June bills.
The new base indices for the PAM are as shown below:
• Foreign Exchange Rate: J$158.11 to us$1.00
• Consumerpricelndex: 141.80
• Electricity charge: J$50.59/kwh.
These revised base indices will remain in effect until the next programmed reset of the ANPAM
in 2026 May, or the implementation of new tariffs, whichever is earlier.

1. Introduction
1.1. On 2025 May 12, RHDL made an application to the OUR for an ANPAM rate adjustment
of 3.62%. The request is consistent with the determination made in the Rose Hall
Utilities Company Limited - Sewerage Rate Determination, Document Number
WAS2011002_DET002, issued on 2011 March 4 (the ``Determination Notice").
1.2. In the Determination Notice, RHDL was granted approval for a PAM component to be a
part of its' rate structure, which consisted of sewerage rates and service charges. The
aim of the mechanism is to correct for movements in the three indices namely, the
Consumer Price Index (Cpl), the Jamaican dollar exchange rate relative to the United
States Dollar (FX) and Electricity Prices (kwh).
1.3. The PAM rate adjustment, which was granted to RHDL, should be equivalent to that of
the NWC's PAM. However, the application of this rate adjustment would have a one-
month lag of the NWC's PAM. Typically the PAM has a feature where there is a reset on
the anniversary date of the Determination Notice. In this case the anniversary date
would be that of the NWC's Determination Notice. This annual reset of the PAM is
termed as the Annual Price Adjustment Mechanism (ANPAM).
1.4. The ANPAM allows for an adjustment of base rates by the rolling-in of the cumulative
monthly PAM rate adjustments into the base rates. The main objective of this annual
reset is to minimize the monthly PAM differential adjustment, which accounts for the
variance between the current and the base values for the three (3) PAM indices on
customers' bills.

2. Legal and Regulatory Framework
2.1. RHDL is regulated by the Office of Utilities Regulation Act and operates under the
following licences (collectively referred to as the Licences):
• Rose Hall Developments Limited watersupply Licence, 2011
• Rose Hall (Developments) Limited sewerage service provider Licence, 2015
2.2. The role and function of the OUR in the water and sewerage sector is governed by
the provisions of the OUR Act. Section 4(1) (a) of the OUR Act, provides that the OUR
•is empowered to ``regulate the provision of prescribed utility services by licensees or
spec/f/.ed organ/.zor/.ons". The provision of sewerage services and the supply and
distribution of water are included among the prescribed utility services defined in the
First Schedule of the OuR Act.
2.3. Section 4(4) of the OUR Act expressly authorizes the OUR to determine the rates
charged for the provision of a prescribed utility service. The section reads:
"(4) The Office shall have power to determine, in accordance with the
provisions of this Act, the rates or fares which may be charged in respect of the
provisions of a prescribed utility service."
2.4. In exercise of its powers to determine rates, the OUR issued the Rose Hall Utilities
Company Limited Sewerage Rate Determination Document No. WAS2011002_DET02
dated 2011 March 04, which sets out the approved rates and charges for RHDL's
sewerage service. The Determination Notice also makes allowance for an annual price
adj.ustment, where RHDL's ANPAM rates are tied to that of the NWC. On 2025 April
28 the Office issued its decision on the NWC's application for an ANPAM rate
adjustment.
2.5. In keeping with the determination regarding the annual reset of the PAM, RHDL has
now applied for an ANPAM rate adjustment of its base rates.

3. OURAnalysisand Determinations
3.1. The OUR's review and determination of rates is guided by the principle of establishing
rates that are sufficient to cover prudently incurred costs. As such, the monthly and
annual price adjustment mechanisms are designed to align RHDL established rates
with input costs that are outside of the company's control.
3.2. The PAM allows RHDL to adjust its rates monthly to account for the effect of changes
in input cost that are exogenous to its operations. It therefore seeks to preserve RHDL
rates in real terms against monthly fluctuations in its input costs, due to changes in
inflation, foreign exchange rate movements and changes in electricity rates.
3.3. The mathematical computation of the PAM is as follows
PAM = (Wfx *AFX + Wcp, *ACpl + Wkwh*Akwh)*100
Where:
AFX is the monthly percentage change in the JS/USS exchange rate,
ACpl is the monthly percentage change in the Cpl,
Akwh is the monthly percentage change in the kilowatt hour charge for
electricity'
wfx is the approved weight for the JS/USS exchange rate,
wcp, is the approved weight for the Cpl, and
wkwh is the approved weight for the kilowatt hour charge for electricity.
3.4. The ANPAM normally allows for an adjustment of base rates and charges each year.
This is achieved by the `rolling- in' of the cumulative PAM rate from the time of last
ANPAM adjustment into the base rates. The calculated ANPAM rate reflects the
weighted change in the base values for the three (3) components in the mechanism,
since the last ANPAM adjustment.
3.5. MathematicaHy, the new base rates may be expressed as follows:
New Base Rate = Current Base Rate * (1 + ANPAM adjustment rate)
3.6. In keeping with the Office's decision to apply an ANPAM rate equivalent to that of
the NWC to the RHDL, the OUR verified the proposed 3.62% ANPAM against the
ANPAM rate that was approved for the NWC.
3.7. The sources of the input data for the ANPAM granted to NWC are as follows:
1. Statistical Institute of Jamaica (STATIN) for Consumer Price Index (Cpl)
2. Bank of Jamaica (BOJ) for foreign exchange (FX) rate (JS:USS); and
3. NWC's electricity bills for the month of 2025 February to ascertain the
electricity component.

3.9. On 2025 April 28, the Office issued the National Water Commission Annual Price
Adjustment Mechanism 2025 Rate Adjustment Determination Notice, Document
Number 2025/WAS/006/DET.001 in which it approved the ANPAM rate adjustment
of 3.62%. The ANPAM rate adjustment will be applied to bills issued by the NWC in
2025 May for services rendered in the month of 2025 April.
3.10.Given the Office's decision in the RHDL's 2011 Determination Notice to align its
ANPAM to that of the NWC, it therefore holds that the approved ANPAM rate
adjustment of 3.62% for the NWC is applicable to RHDL. Accordingly, in keeping with
the Determination Notice, the current baseline rates as shown in Table 3.1 above,
shall be adjusted to reflect the new baseline parameters of FX: $158.11, Cpl: 141.80
and Electricity: $50.59/kwh. This translates to the base rates adjustment of 3.62%.
3.11.The new base sewerage rates for RHDL are displayed in Table 3.2 below. The
approved sewerage rates will become effective on customers' 2025 June bills.
3.12.In the 2011 Determination Notice, no approval was granted for rates to ``primary
schools". Consequently, RHDL's request for the ANPAM rate adjustment to be applied
to primary school rates is not approved.
